intro: I love working on the customer journey, understanding the problems customers face, and building products that solve them.

decision: The one number that says the booking page worked
options: Share of students who book again within 14 days of a first booking
Count of bookings per week
Share of page visitors who complete a booking
recommendation: Share of students who book again within 14 days of a first booking
reason: The page earns its keep by making coming back to class easy, so repeat booking says it worked better than raw volume.
question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week?

decision: What we measure at Book and pay
options: Booking completions divided by booking starts, per class
Count of payments taken per week
Time from picking a class to confirmed payment
recommendation: Booking completions divided by booking starts, per class
reason: It shows exactly where students drop out of the booking flow and which classes struggle.

decision: What we measure at Find a class
options: Share of visits that reach a class choice or Book your usual within one session
Count of page views
Search and filter usage counts
recommendation: Share of visits that reach a class choice or Book your usual within one session
reason: It tells us whether students can find a class quickly, which is the first promise of the page.

decision: What we measure and keep at Show up
options: Attended vs booked per class, kept as a count with the booking record
Attendance by named student kept indefinitely
No attendance tracking
recommendation: Attended vs booked per class, kept as a count with the booking record
reason: No-show rate per class shows whether reminders work and whether the waitlist should fill spots, without extra personal data.

note: Data craft: one measure per journey step plus the single page-level success number, keeping only what a decision would use.

text: Theo: data craft: one measure per journey step plus the single page-level success number, keeping only what a decis….

decision: What booking should feel like for a student
options: Quick and remembered: regulars see their usual class first
Guided and reassuring: step by step with confirmations
recommendation: Quick and remembered: regulars see their usual class first
reason: One filled button marks the main action, so the grey wireframes lead with a single 'Book your usual' path and a plain class list for newcomers beneath it.
question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week, and how should booking support that?

decision: What leads the class list and how dense it is
options: Next seven days grouped by day, one line per class
Cards per class with teacher and level
Week grid like a timetable
recommendation: Next seven days grouped by day, one line per class
reason: Single-column rows keep the page uncluttered and thumb-friendly at 390px, with 44px tap targets and one card recipe.

decision: What a full class shows and offers
options: Show 'Full' with a Join the waitlist button
Hide full classes
Show 'Full' with no action
recommendation: Show 'Full' with a Join the waitlist button
reason: A visible full state with a clear verb-and-object button keeps students from guessing, and the waitlist state is designed as a full screen state rather than an error.
question: If a class is full, what would a student want to happen next?

decision: Which single accent colour the page uses
options: Warm clay on paper
Soft sage green on paper
recommendation: Warm clay on paper
reason: The interface stays 90 to 95% neutral with one accent, and clay reads calm and warm, never violet, with ink text for 7:1 contrast.

note: Listed four design decisions for the yoga booking page: the feel of the flow, what leads the class list, the full-class state, and the single accent.

text: Mika: listed four design decisions for the yoga booking page: the feel of the flow, what leads the class list, the….

decision: Who the page serves first: regulars or newcomers
options: Regulars rebooking their usual
Newcomers booking a first class
Both equally
recommendation: Regulars rebooking their usual
reason: A small studio lives on people coming back, so we'd first learn how regulars book today and where it frustrates them.
question: What makes someone come back to a yoga class week after week?

decision: Whether full classes get a waitlist
options: Waitlist with a cutoff on late cancellations
No waitlist, just show full
Waitlist with no cutoff
recommendation: Waitlist with a cutoff on late cancellations
reason: One leisure provider (Active Monash) runs a waitlist and stops cancellations within 1 hour of start so waitlisted people can get there, though we have no data on how often people get a spot and the page was unverified.
question: How should it feel for a student to find a class they wanted is already full?

Fewer empty spots in classes
Fewer front-desk messages

decision: What happens when two students take the last spot at once
options: First confirmed booking wins; the other sees 'just filled' and is offered the waitlist
Hold the spot for a few minutes while the student pays
Allow overbooking and let the studio sort it out
recommendation: First confirmed booking wins; the other sees 'just filled' and is offered the waitlist
reason: The server checks the spot count when confirming, which is plain, proven, and means a confirmed spot is never taken away.
question: How should it feel for a student who loses the last spot to someone else a second earlier?

decision: Whether full classes get a waitlist
options: Waitlist on, with automatic offer when a spot opens
Waitlist off, show 'Full' only
Waitlist on, studio promotes people manually
recommendation: Waitlist on, with automatic offer when a spot opens
reason: The template has a waitlist switch, and automatic offers avoid empty mats without staff work.

decision: What a student must give to book, and whether this device remembers them
options: Name and email only, remember me on this device
Name, email and phone, remember me on this device
Full account with password
recommendation: Name and email only, remember me on this device
reason: No passwords means fewer failure points, and remembering the device makes booking your usual quick for regulars.
question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week, and what should the page ask of them to keep that easy?

label: Book your usual
reason: No passwords means fewer failure points, and remembering the device makes booking your usual quick for regulars.

What the page does when payment or confirmation fails
options: Show a clear message, keep the spot unbooked, let them retry, and never charge twice
Hold the spot and email a payment link
Show a generic error and ask them to contact the studio
recommendation: Show a clear message, keep the spot unbooked, let them retry, and never charge twice
reason: A failed step should leave a clean state with no double charge, and the confirmation email or text is sent only after the booking is saved.

decision: Who the page serves first: regulars or newcomers
options: Regulars rebooking their usual
Newcomers finding a first class
Both equally
recommendation: Regulars rebooking their usual
reason: A small studio lives on people coming back weekly, so the page earns its keep by making rebooking take a few taps, while newcomers still get a plain path through Pick one.
question: What makes someone come back to a studio week after week, and who is that person for you?

decision: What happens when a class is full
options: Offer a waitlist with automatic spot offer
Show full with no waitlist
Waitlist that only notifies, with no hold
recommendation: Offer a waitlist with automatic spot offer
reason: A full class is a common frustration and a waitlist turns it into a kept booking, but the student must know clearly how long they have to claim a freed spot.
question: How should it feel for a student who finds their favourite class already full?

decision: How students pay when booking
options: Pay at booking by card or pass
Reserve free and pay at the studio
Both, with studio choosing per class
recommendation: Pay at booking by card or pass
reason: Payment up front makes the held spot feel trustworthy and reduces no-shows, and class passes can be spent in the same step.
question: When a student books, what would make them feel sure their spot is truly theirs?

decision: Cancellation and late-cancel rule shown to students
options: Free cancel until a set cutoff, then pass is used
Free cancel any time
No cancellations
recommendation: Free cancel until a set cutoff, then pass is used
reason: A clear cutoff protects the teacher from empty mats while staying fair, and it must be stated in plain words at booking and in the reminder.
question: What would feel fair to your students when they can't make a class they booked?

note: Drafted the core journey decisions for the yoga studio booking page: who it serves first, full-class handling, payment at booking, and cancellation rules.

decision: Whether students pay online when booking or at the studio
options: Pay online to book
Pay at the studio
Online or at the studio, student's choice
recommendation: Pay online to book
reason: A paid spot is a held spot, so students trust it and the studio sees fewer no-shows, and it makes the book-and-pay step work end to end.
question: What would make a student feel sure their spot is truly theirs the moment they book?

decision: How classes are sold: drop-in, class packs, or membership
options: Single drop-in only
Drop-in plus class packs
Drop-in, packs and monthly membership
recommendation: Drop-in plus class packs
reason: Newcomers need a low-commitment first class and regulars want a cheaper repeat rate, while membership can wait for evidence.
question: How do newcomers and regulars each want to commit to a studio, and what changes when they come back week after week?

decision: What happens to a student's money when they cancel or miss a class, and when the studio cancels
options: Free cancel up to a cutoff, then credit lost; studio cancels refund in full
Always credit back to the pass, never cash
Strict no refunds
recommendation: Free cancel up to a cutoff, then credit lost; studio cancels refund in full
reason: A clear, fair rule protects the studio's empty-spot risk while keeping students confident to book, and it is a promise once students rely on it.
question: When a student's plans change at the last minute, what would feel fair to them and to the studio?

decision: Whether first-time students get an intro offer
options: No intro offer, same price for all
Discounted first class
Free or discounted intro week
recommendation: Discounted first class
reason: Why now: the page needs newcomers to try a class, and a small first-visit price lowers the risk of booking a stranger's studio.
question: What stops a curious newcomer from booking their very first class?
